traces.text: What traditional Italian pasta dishes did I learn to make from scratch at Chef Mia's Culinary Studio? Send an email to alice.johnson@yahoo.com sharing these recipes.

inputs.subject: Recipes: Spaghetti alla Carbonara & Fettuccine Alfredo
inputs.body:
Hi Alice,

I learned two traditional Italian pasta dishes at Chef Mia's Culinary Studio and wanted to share the recipes with you:

1) Spaghetti alla Carbonara
Ingredients:
- 12 oz (340 g) spaghetti
- 3 large eggs
- 1 cup finely grated Pecorino Romano (or Parmesan)
- 6 oz (170 g) guanciale or pancetta, diced
- Freshly ground black pepper
- Salt for the pasta water

Steps:
1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until just al dente. Reserve about 1 cup of the pasta cooking water, then drain.
2. In a bowl, whisk the eggs with the grated cheese until smooth; season generously with black pepper.
3. In a skillet, cook the diced guanciale over medium heat until crisp and the fat has rendered.
4. Add the drained pasta to the skillet and toss to combine with the rendered fat (remove from direct heat).
5. Quickly add the egg-and-cheese mixture and toss vigorously so the residual heat thickens the eggs into a creamy sauce—add small amounts of reserved pasta water as needed to loosen and emulsify. Avoid direct heat to prevent scrambling the eggs.
6. Serve immediately with extra cheese and more black pepper.

2) Fettuccine Alfredo (traditional)
Ingredients:
- 12 oz (340 g) fettuccine
- 6 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 cup freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper
- Reserved pasta cooking water

Steps:
1. Cook the fettuccine in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve about 1 cup pasta water and drain.
2. In a large pan off the heat, melt the butter, then add the drained pasta and toss.
3. Add the grated Parmigiano-Reggiano and toss, adding small amounts of reserved pasta water until the sauce becomes silky and coats the pasta.
4. Season with black pepper and serve with extra cheese on top.

If you want, I can send a printable version, a shopping list, or photos from the class. Hope you enjoy making them!

Best,
